description: [1/5] Plan: pure C++17 core (include lexer state machine, dependency graph, cycle/cost analysis, deterministic report rendering) + imperative CLI shell with all I/O at the edges; 5 bounded milestones, each test-green alone.

impact_assessment.why: Programmers working in C++ have no zero-dependency tool that makes header coupling explicit, finds include cycles, and recommends forward declarations; the portfolio covers FSM verification (Sextant) and architecture conformance (Limen) but not C++ include hygiene.
impact_assessment.benefits: A deterministic, offline analyzer whose pure core is reusable and whose CLI is a drop-in CI check with stable, reproducible output.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CLI flags and report schema; dependency: none (C++17 stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: lexer and DFS must be explicit state machines, not hidden recursion with mutable globals.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Encode the lexer and DFS as enum state machines with pure transition functions; fail-first unit tests for every state transition; integration tests via the built binary; run aikit check knot before any commit.

description: [2/5] Functional core: 15-state include lexer, iterative DFS cycle detector, identifier scanner, transitive-cost worklist, deterministic text/JSON renderers; 74 unit checks green.
[3/5] Imperative shell: pure argv decoder, filesystem/stdout I/O confined to files.cpp, main wiring with exit codes 0/1/2/3; scripts/test.cmd builds and smokes the binary.
[4/5] README prerequisites/tree, ADR-001, regenerated codebase map, 3 AIKit audit reports; all five gates pass (hygiene, guidelines, secrets, compat, test).
Task 'knot-include-graph' completed successfully.

description: [1/5] Plan: add shortest include-path queries (knot why), a pure JSON snapshot reader and deterministic baseline diff (knot diff), plus CI thresholds; keep core pure and all stateful traversals as explicit state machines.

impact_assessment.why: Finding a cycle is only half the job: programmers need to know the exact chain that pulls a header in, and CI needs to detect that header coupling grew since a recorded baseline.
impact_assessment.benefits: Actionable 'why is this header here' answers and a golden-baseline regression gate that makes include-graph growth visible before it lands.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new CLI flags and a versioned snapshot schema; dependency: none (C++17 stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: BFS and JSON lexing must be explicit state machines, not hidden mutable state.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure BFS/json_step/transition functions with deterministic tie-breaking; property test that render_json output parses back to the same snapshot; fail-first tests for diff verdicts; full AIKit gate run before commit.

description: [2/5] Pure core additions: BFS path state machine, JSON lexer + parser, snapshot/diff model, include resolution for absolute roots; 115 checks green.

description: [1/5] Plan: add reverse impact analysis (who is affected when a header changes) and DOT/Mermaid graph export; both pure, both with explicit state machines and deterministic output.

impact_assessment.why: A cycle report tells you a header is tangled, but a maintainer needs the reverse closure to know what to rebuild and retest, plus a visual export to review coupling with other people.
impact_assessment.benefits: Impact sets make blast radius explicit before a header edit; DOT/Mermaid export makes the graph reviewable in CI artifacts and documentation without adding a dependency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two new subcommands and two export formats; dependency: none (C++17 stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: reverse BFS must be an explicit state machine with deterministic ordering.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure reverse-graph construction and impact_step state machine; golden output tests for DOT/Mermaid; snapshot the exact output in tests; run all AIKit gates before commit.

description: [1/5] Plan: add a pure glob state machine and .knotignore parsing (including negation), applied at the filesystem edge so real C++ trees can exclude generated and vendor directories.

impact_assessment.why: Hardcoded skips for .git/build/node_modules do not match real repositories, so scans were noisy and could report coupling from generated or vendored code.
impact_assessment.benefits: Programmers can scope an analysis to the code they own, and the same rule set applies to scan, why, impact, diff and graph.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: .knotignore syntax and CLI --ignore flag; dependency: none (C++17 stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: glob matching must be an explicit backtracking state machine with deterministic semantics.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure glob_step with bounded backtracking; golden tests for '*', '**', '?', directory rules and negation; smoke test on a fixture with an ignored directory; all AIKit gates before commit.

description: [1/5] Plan: add a pure policy model and a 'knot check' preset that applies cycle/cost/hotspot limits and an optional baseline regression in one command.

impact_assessment.why: The individual CI flags are useful but a project needs one stable command whose policy lives in the repository, so a check cannot silently change when a runner's flags change.
impact_assessment.benefits: A single reproducible CI entry point with a versioned policy file; violations are reported as a deterministic list with text and JSON output.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: .knot-policy key/value schema and new subcommand; dependency: none (C++17 stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: policy parsing and violation evaluation must be pure.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure parse_policy/evaluate_policy with golden tests for each limit and for boolean/whitespace parsing; smoke the full command on a fixture; run all gates before commit.

description: [1/5] Plan: add advisory detection of used types whose defining internal header is not reachable from the translation unit, reusing the pure identifier scanner and path query.

impact_assessment.why: A very common C++ error is using a type whose header was never included (or was only included transitively elsewhere); compilers report it far from the cause.
impact_assessment.benefits: Actionable 'consider including X.hpp' advice derived from the same inspectable graph, with no compiler or third-party tooling.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new recommendation kind and render label; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the analysis stays pure and uses the existing path query.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Advisory-only wording, restrict candidates to scanned headers and exact type identifiers, golden tests for included vs missing cases, full gates before commit.

[4/5] README, ADR-006, map and consolidated audit updated; 5/5 gates pass and 164 checks green.
Task 'knot-missing-includes' completed successfully.

description: [1/4] Plan: add knot init to write starter .knotignore and .knot-policy, keeping content generation pure and file writes at the edge.

impact_assessment.why: A new user has to discover the policy and ignore file syntax before getting value; zero-friction onboarding is part of the architectural brief.
impact_assessment.benefits: One command produces a documented starting point that the user can edit; content is generated by a pure function so it is testable without touching disk.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two generated files and --force semantics; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: generation is pure, writes guarded so existing files are never overwritten silently.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden content tests, refusal on existing files without --force, smoke in a temp directory, full gate run before commit.

description: [1/4] Plan: add knot baseline <dir> <file> [--force] that writes a complete JSON snapshot from a pure renderer, with an overwrite guard at the I/O edge.

impact_assessment.why: Regressions are only useful if a reviewed state can be promoted to the new baseline; requiring manual shell redirection invites truncated or stale baselines.
impact_assessment.benefits: A complete, deterministic baseline in one command, protected from accidental overwrite, with the same round-trip guarantees as scan --format json.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new subcommand and complete-snapshot renderer; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: generation stays pure, write guarded.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure render_baseline_json with a round-trip test that every node is captured; refuse overwrite without --force; smoke on a fixture; full gates before commit.
